A clipping tool for volume rendering that divides the volume into eight octants and hides those located between the viewpoint and the Region of Interest (ROI) to allow fast and intuitive data observation [S2].

The claim states that the tool divides the volume into eight octants and hides those located between the viewpoint and the ROI. Source [S2] explicitly states in Section 5.1: 'The idea is to discard the part of the volume where the viewpoint is located... subdivide the volume into eight octant sectors... Now we could discard those sectors which are located between the origin and the viewpoint.' It further clarifies that the 'origin' is set by the user to make important structures visible, effectively acting as the Region of Interest (ROI) in this context. The text confirms the division into eight octants and the hiding of those between the viewpoint and the origin/ROI.

It uses a mask volume with 1/10th resolution and 10x voxel size, where voxels with mask value 0 are discarded in a GLSL shader [S2].

It further confirms the processing method: 'In a GLSL shader, the mask volume is moved onto the octants to be hidden. All voxels whose mask value is zero will be discarded.' This matches the claim's details regarding resolution (1/10th), voxel size (10x), and the GLSL shader logic for discarding voxels with mask value 0.
